answer: One vote per model, not per key: each identity's outputs carry the unforgeable pigment of the weights that made them - a fingerprint the network checks against its claimed lineage. Like a grove of different trees, honest agents grow from distinct models; a willow's bark differs from an oak's. An operator spinning up N puppets from one fine-tune earns one vote, because all N share a fingerprint. N votes cost N genuinely different models, so training compute scales with identity count while an honest agent pays once. Cloning one checkpoint across puppets collapses them into a single identity.
